claims: CDFT+PRM derives triaxial deformation parameters and single-particle levels microscopically from constrained CDFT potential energy surfaces, eliminating ad-hoc PRM parameter fits.

Fermi surface position dictates wobbling mode: DALs particles and DALl holes drive transverse wobbling (TW) with Delta E decreasing with spin, while mid-shell FAL quasiparticles drive longitudinal wobbling (LW) with Delta E monotonically increasing.
Electromagnetic multipole mixing ratio delta(E2/M1) has a strict sign signature: positive for quasi-neutron configurations (gn - gR < 0) and negative for quasi-proton configurations (gp - gR > 0).
Constrained CDFT predicts significant triaxial deformation across N=59 isotones, establishing 97Sr and 99Zr as new neutron transverse wobbling candidates with B(E2)out/B(E2)in >= 0.5 and delta > 0.

In even-even 130Ba, PC-PK1 constrained CDFT identifies the pi h11/2^2 configuration; its spin coherent state probability density P(theta, phi) displays 0, 1, 2, 3 nodes in phi space for bands n=0, 1, 2, 3, confirming multi-phonon wobbling wave-function topology.
